title: PVWA Overview and Administration
content:
The Password Vault Web Access (PVWA) provides a web interface for managing privileged accounts in CyberArk Privilege Cloud and PAM Self-Hosted deployments. Administrators access PVWA at https://<pvwa-server>/PasswordVault.

## Key Features

- Privileged account discovery and onboarding
- Password rotation and verification policies
- Session monitoring and recording
- Access control workflows with dual control and ticketing integration
- Platform management for target systems
- Reports and audit trails

## Architecture

PVWA communicates with the Vault server through the Central Policy Manager (CPM) and Privileged Session Manager (PSM). All credentials are stored encrypted in the Digital Vault, never in PVWA itself.

## Common Administration Tasks

### Resetting the PVWA Admin Password

1. Connect to the PVWA server via RDP
2. Open the PVWA Configuration tool (PVConfiguration.exe)
3. Navigate to the Administration section
4. Select Reset Admin Password
5. Follow the wizard to set a new password
6. Restart the CyberArk Vault service

### Configuring LDAP Integration

1. Log into PVWA as an administrator
2. Navigate to Administration > LDAP Integration
3. Add a new LDAP directory with your domain controller details
4. Map LDAP groups to CyberArk Safes and permissions
5. Test the connection before saving

### Managing Safes

Safes are the primary access control boundary in CyberArk. Each safe contains accounts and is assigned owners with specific permissions.

To create a Safe:
```
POST /PasswordVault/api/Safes
{
  "SafeName": "Linux-Production",
  "Description": "Production Linux root accounts",
  "ManagingCPM": "CPM_01",
  "NumberOfDaysRetention": 30
}
```

## PVWA Error Codes

| Error Code | Description | Resolution |
|---|---|---|
| ITATS001E | Session timeout | Clear browser cache and re-authenticate |
| PVWA401 | Authentication failed | Verify credentials and LDAP integration |
| PASWS034E | Safe not found | Check Safe permissions in PrivateArk |
| PASWS036E | Account locked | Wait for lockout period or unlock in PrivateArk |
| PVWA500 | Internal server error | Check IIS application pool and CyberArk services |

## API Authentication

PVWA REST API supports multiple authentication methods:

### CyberArk Authentication
```bash
curl -X POST https://pvwa.example.com/PasswordVault/api/auth/CyberArk/Logon \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"username": "admin", "password": "P@ssw0rd"}'
```

### LDAP Authentication
```bash
curl -X POST https://pvwa.example.com/PasswordVault/api/auth/LDAP/Logon \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"username": "admin@domain.com", "password": "P@ssw0rd"}'
```

## Performance Tuning

- Set IIS application pool recycling to off-hours
- Configure connection pooling for Vault connections
- Use load balancing across multiple PVWA instances
- Enable compression for API responses
- Monitor IIS worker process memory usage
